newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANUCKS ANNOUNCE SIGNING OF MESSIER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANUCKS ANNOUNCE SIGNING OF MESSIER.

text.p: Mark Messier, who led the New York Rangers to their first Stanley Cup in 54 years in 1994, is moving on to a new challenge after signing a rich, three-year deal on Monday with the Vancouver Canucks.
Various reports said that Messier's deal was worth at least $20 million and also included an incentive package that could add substantially to the overall value of the contract.

The 36-year-old Messier, regarded as one of the best leaders in team sports, had 36 goals and 48 assists for 84 points last season in the final year of a three-year, $18 million contract with the Rangers.

The Rangers offered Messier, who also won five Stanley Cups earlier in his career with the Edmonton Oilers, a two-year deal worth $10 million with an option for a third year, but it was not enough to retain their captain.
"It's a sad day in New York," Madison Square Garden President Dave Checketts told WFAN Radio in New York Monday.
"I wanted him to finish his career in New York. We thought there was a level of trust that clearly did not exist. We did not get a chance to make one last pitch. We never made our best offer."

The Canucks may have been out for revenge after losing to the Rangers in the 1994 Stanley Cup Finals. They lost again to New York in the Wayne Gretzky sweepstakes last summer, when the Rangers signed the Great One.
But the Canucks struck gold at the expense of the Rangers this time with a whopping offer to Messier.
The Canucks missed the playoffs last season by going 35-40-7 for 77 points, and had trouble filling GM Place, their new arena.

Aiming for someone to bring out the best in inconsistent star Russian wingers Pavel Bure and Alexander Mogilny, the Canucks have turned to Messier. They now can boast two top lines that will include, among others, Messier, Bure, Mogilny and the current team captain, Trevor Linden.
In 18 NHL seasons with Edmonton and the Rangers, Messier is 10th all-time in goals with 575, sixth in assists with 977 and fifth in points with 1,552.

A ferocious two-way player, Messier won the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP for the Oilers in 1984. He also won the Hart Trophy, given to the league's MVP, in 1990 with Edmonton and 1992 with the Rangers.
Messier teamed with Gretzky on the Oilers dynasty of the 1980s, but led Edmonton to the 1990 Stanley Cup after Gretzky's departure.

Though he suffered through one of the worst playoff performances of his career last season, scoring three goals with nine assists in 15 games, Messier is still second to Gretzky among all-time post-season performers with 109 goals, 186 assists and 295 points.
